clue.text: Very good holes in the ground for birds

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation of pious, i.e. very good
pits are holes dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Something excellent: hollows in the earth where birds can nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipits are small brown songbirds, so the plural noun fits the plural birds.

clue.text: Quietly step up for worship

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly
to step up something is to raise or increase it

explanation.surface: An instruction to a congregation to rise softly for a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are nouns or verbs for glorifying God, as in hymns of adoration.

clue.text: Sets forth as defender of imperial units

parts.note: a pro is someone in favour, a supporter or defender of a cause
pounds are units of weight in the old British imperial system

explanation.surface: Someone presents himself as a champion of the old non-metric weights and measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound a theory is to put it forward or set it out for consideration.

clue.text: Picture of item of furniture with gold

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A painting of a piece of gilded furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or group, a living picture.

clue.text: Tea is provided by mum — an appealing quality

parts.note: char is a colloquial British word for tea, from the Chinese cha
ma is another word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother making the tea is a lovely trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal charm or attractiveness that draws others.

clue.text: A hated No. 2 in school here replaced his/her boss?

indicators.note: letters replaced, put back in a different place, signal rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: number two in a word is its second letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detested deputy head at a school who has ousted the person above them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 2 in school' does double duty in the surface as a deputy head; mechanically it is just the second letter C of school, shuffled with A HATED and HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a school's deputy (its No. 2) reports to is the head of the school.

clue.text: Platform with men turning up to play guitar?

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers or men
to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: A stage on which a band of men appear, ready to strum some chords.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: Group of soldiers in snake-like formation on square?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the letter S has the winding shape of a snake
a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard

explanation.surface: Troops snaking their way across a parade square.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a small unit of soldiers drilled or working together.

clue.text: Pub, a terrible hole to resort to

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad, messed-up state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to resort to a thing is to use it

explanation.surface: A dreadful dive of a tavern that one is nonetheless forced to frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is an old-fashioned word for a tavern serving beer.

clue.text: A crowd crossing middle of field by a very small animal

indicators.note: a crowd crossing a field puts the field's letter within the crowd

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A mob trampling across a meadow beside a tiny creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled microscopic organism, classed among the simplest animals.

clue.text: Susan's about to be entertained by European ballerina

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host sits inside the host's home, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

indicators.note: about signals turning the piece around, reading it backwards

parts.note: Sue is short for Susan, so Susan's is Sue's

explanation.surface: Susan is about to be hosted by someone from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'about to be' as 'going to be'; in fact 'about' turns Sue's backwards to SEUS, and 'to be entertained by' puts that inside the Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseuse is the French-derived word for a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Bird, one a short time outside church at end of street

indicators.note: the rest is placed after the abbreviation for street
these letters are placed around the church abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation of time

explanation.surface: A bird, alone briefly outside a church at the end of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' and 'at end of' look like scene-setting places, but each places pieces: the church sits within one-a-time, and all that follows the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small European songbird whose call sounds like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Scary procedure to create a beehive?

definitions.meaning: frightening enough to make one's hair stand on end
a beehive is a tall piled-up hairdo, made by lifting the hair high

explanation.surface: A frightening process for building a home for bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Scary things are said to make your hair stand up, and a beehive hairstyle literally lifts the hair.

clue.text: Message over the air, star's last farewell cut short

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
something cut short loses its end letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, a farewell

explanation.surface: A broadcast of a celebrity's final goodbye, abruptly interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: To radio is to send a message by wireless transmission through the air.

clue.text: Minutes north or south on a sea journey

definitions.text: Minutes north or south on a sea journey

parts.words: Minutes north or south on a sea journey
parts.note: one minute of arc of latitude, measured north or south, is the unit of distance used by sailors at sea

explanation.surface: Time spent sailing up or down the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' suggests time, but here it means sixtieths of a degree of latitude, each of which is one unit of distance at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea unit of distance is defined as one minute of latitude, about 1,852 metres.

clue.text: Piglet struggling with nut is slackening

indicators.note: struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little pig wrestling with a nut eventually eases off.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting up means easing off or relaxing effort, the same as becoming slack.

clue.text: Beset by awful brutes, act to construct defences

indicators.note: something beset by others is surrounded by them, so it goes inside
awful suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: Surrounded by savage thugs, one must get on with building fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges the thugs to REUBTS, and 'Beset by' puts the verb for act inside them; 'to construct' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubts are small enclosed fortifications, outworks for defence.

clue.text: Way to go that's briefly provided by seven experts

definitions.text: Way to go that's briefly provided by seven experts

parts.words: Way to go that's briefly provided by seven experts
parts.note: the compass bearing between east and north-east is abbreviated to three letters, which sit inside the words seven experts

explanation.surface: A route recommended in shorthand by a panel of seven specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-letter compass abbreviation ENE lies inside 'sevEN Experts', and 'briefly' says that this short form is the answer. The grammar cannot express expanding an abbreviation, so it is shown as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass direction is a way to head, here the point midway between east and north-east.

clue.text: Smarter gossip that takes one in

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another
completes the phrase takes in, marking the inner piece

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sharper chatterbox who swallows whatever she is told.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smart, so the comparative means smarter.

clue.text: Chemical one found outside school

indicators.note: one piece is found around the outside of another

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A substance discovered just beyond the school gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a colourless solvent, a common chemical in nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Writer of detective stories? Right!

definitions.meaning: Colin ... wrote the Inspector Morse detective novels
in heraldry the term for the right-hand side of a shield

explanation.surface: Guessing an author of whodunits and being told you are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is both the Morse novelist and a Latin-derived word for right-hand.

clue.text: Attack supported by 13?

parts.note: something on another is supported by it
the answer to 13 across is a wireless, which is a receiving set

explanation.surface: An offensive backed by the clue at 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of an assault, an attack.

clue.text: Stick people in a firm?

definitions.meaning: a stout pole or rod carried for walking or as a symbol of office
employees, the personnel of a company

explanation.surface: Telling workers to remain with a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff is both a walking stick and the workforce of an organisation.

clue.text: Follower of Moses — a sir possibly 'chosen'?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the elite are the chosen few

explanation.surface: A disciple of Moses, perhaps a knight, among the chosen people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A SIR into ISRA. 'chosen' echoes the chosen people, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Israelites were the Hebrew people whom Moses led out of Egypt.

clue.text: Capital in trouble is suffering setback after initial support

indicators.note: the rest comes after the opening piece, which is placed first

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A capital city in difficulty, with fortunes reversed after early backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' reverses AILIS to SILIA, placed after BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasília is the purpose-built capital of Brazil.

clue.text: Nothing looked for after initial change of direction

indicators.note: the opening compass letter, south, is switched to north

parts.note: sought is the past tense of seek, to look for

explanation.surface: Searching yielded nothing after the first change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A nought is zero, the figure meaning nothing.

clue.text: Without hesitation, put up with anger — it's sort of right

indicators.note: without means losing these letters from the word

parts.note: to suffer is to tolerate or put up with
er is the sound of hesitation
rage is fury, anger

explanation.surface: Unhesitatingly bearing one's fury, it's somewhat justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffrage is the right to vote, one particular kind of entitlement.

clue.text: Season in which lord keeps very quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman or lord
PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: A time of year when an aristocrat keeps his peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a noun for a time of year; it is the verb, to flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper food is to season it with the ground spice.
